Metaxy

by OneStoryAfterAnother

Summary

Mydei and Phainon learn to love not through declarations, but through quiet gestures. Their bond is never named, only felt—traced in wounds, accompanied in silence, and sealed beneath starlight.

Fragment of Reconciliation: Okhema Holy City, Year ████.

“If I didn’t know any better I'd say you love me.” Phainon teasing tone hanging on at the end, lingering a few seconds more as if reading into Mydei’s soul. Mydei stiffened. Silence taking the place in exchange for conversation.

“Mmh.”

“Is that a yes?”

“I’ll tell you in our next life.”

“I’ll look forward to it then.”

Or:
They never name what they are. They just keep choosing each other in every quiet moment. Moments unmarked by history in the Hero’s epics.

Notes

Scattered across Amphoreus, left by the passage of time, are Fragments of Reconciliation. They are said to capture stories of the past and encapsulate them, preserving memories of yesteryear days. Many know stories of Amphoreus’s named heroes, Lord Phainon and Crown Prince Mydeimos. But none of their affinity, camaraderie, and romance—unmarked by history. All that’s left of their love, lives in memories.

See the end of the work for more notes

Fragment of Reconciliation: Okhema Holy City, Year 4930, Month of Strife. 

‧︵‿₊୨☾୧₊‿︵‧ 

Returning from battle is an unspoken crime. A dishonor to the people of Castrum Kremnos. Yet, the Crown Prince Mydeimos returns every time. There’s a trail of golden blood entering the gates of Okhema. Golden ichor, ethereal as it may be, shining its yellow hues in Okhema’s light. It was during the rise of Action Hour, when Mydeimos had returned. His right shoulder blade and bicep carried a cavernous gash, cutting deeply into the flesh—as if by a single, fluid motion.

Mydeimos—who is either indifferent to the spilling ichor, or so accustomed to pain—that he failed to notice the divine blood threading down his body after battle. He walks the city gates, taking wary steps to his chambers as swiftly as possible. He halts before he turns the last corner. The air stills his movement, the sound of his clothing fabric jousting before fading. The clink of his heel stops with a sharp pause. Mydeimos can hear people coming from his direction and retreats. He takes a step back instantaneously and another, grazing his right shoulder against the wall—suddenly making his wound ache in a vicious throb that makes him clutch the injury.

Mydeimos hissed. The voices from before grew louder, and from where Mydeimos stood, he could hear idle chatter begin to walk in the direction of his vicinity. In a panic to not be discovered in such a frantic state, Mydeimos spots a door covered in ivy vines hiding behind rows of stone pillars. Once Mydeimos enters through the door, he closes his eyes—to ease the pain in his shoulder or out of pure relief at not being seen—hearing the footsteps and chatter slowly fade into the background.

The realization that Mydeimos is bleeding comes to him when he goes to move his arm—the one clutching the wound—that he spots his golden blood treading down his forearm, cascading down into ribbons, dripping down his elbow.

Oh.

An ink of gold drops onto the prestige stone flooring, so vivid that it stands out. Mydeimos let out a breath of distress, knocking his head against the door he leaned back on. The cooling surface of stone tensing the skin on his open back. Mydeimos opens his eyes and sees the room he is in. It has a simple bed with a wooden desk sitting across from it. In front of him was a balcony, translucent white curtains hanging loosely, brushing against the breeze.

He feels his blood slip through the cracks of his fingers and looks down to inspect his wound. A noise of irritation left Mydeimos’s mouth, more so out of annoyance than actual pain.

How troublesome.

Perhaps he could look for Hyacine in the Garden of Life, but he decides against it, not wanting to bother her with his troubles. After all, he was the one who managed to get injured in battle. It is his fault and he alone should deal with it. To Mydeimos, who has been left alone never knowing love from his father and being too young to remember his mother’s love, Mydeimos did not know love—especially in one's own self.

Mydeimos makes his way to the wooden desk, taking off his gauntlets and setting them down. The metal slides against the surface with a small clash. With his hand now off his wound, the river of blood flows down even harder. Mydeimos can see the discoloration of the dried blood—blood that is not only his but of the creatures of the black tides.

His hand grabbed the edge of the table. Failing to notice the breeze that enters the room with the opening of the door.

Mydeimos doesn’t look up, head turned downwards. His hair sticks to the side of his face from the sweat and grime, falling in frames to hide his expression. The initial adrenaline rush must have worn off because suddenly the pain is so intense, Mydeimos feels his head grow fuzzy. The grip on the table tightens slightly and that causes his gash to bleed even more.

“Mydei..?”

The voice that speaks his name is soft with a hint of surprise in it before cutting off. It snaps Mydeimos out of his trance and he blinks slowly, turning to meet the figure at the door.

Phainon.

Phainon doesn’t say anything and Mydeimos’s eyes narrow, eyeing the man down. He doesn’t know the expression he is wearing, but by the way Phainon's smile slightly drops, he thinks he must be doing a bad job of looking composed and untroubled.

They simply stare at each other in silence, unmoving. Mydeimos turns his gaze back to the floor, his peripheral quickly growing blurry. He hears the door close with a click and Mydeimos thinks that Phainon has left.

Then footsteps make their way across the room and stop right before Mydeimos. A hand extends out and he glances up to see a hand holding a handkerchief out towards him. Even now, they don’t say anything. Phainon simply stares, not wearing his usual plastered grin. In its place is a small, transient smile. Mydeimos reaches out for it, only for Phainon to retreat his hand back, as if taunting him.

“Deliverer… if this is your idea of fun then I beg to differ.” Mydeimos’s voice strained, trying to keep his false sense of anger within it. But Mydeimos was not angry, no, he was confused about why Phainon was still here.

Why didn’t you leave? he wanted to ask. But he refrained, he knew better than to ask.

“You understand me wrong, Mydei. I wish to help you. That is all.” And Mydeimos’s eyebrows raise at his response.

Mydeimos then finally moves, shifting his body to face Phainon and look him in the eyes. Phainon takes a step closer and Mydeimos warily pulls back. His voice came out so low that Phainon almost didn’t hear it.

“I do not wish to dirty you with my blood, Deliverer.” And Phainon let out a quiet, mirthful breath.

“Let it dirty me. I’ll wear it.” Phainon goes to place his hand on Mydeimos’s shoulder, hovering over it, not quite touching. “May I..?” Mydeimos reluctantly nods and Phainon takes his wrist, pulling him in the direction of the bed. Phainon makes Mydeimos sit on the bedding before allowing himself to kneel on the floor, tending to a wound that is fragile and all the more his own. The chamber of the room is accompanied by the winds, swaying the curtains inwards. It casts a chill all throughout and threads through Mydeimos’s hair. Phainon finds distraction in Mydeimos’s lure.

Ichor stains his shelves as Phainon takes Mydeimos’s hand in his own, caressing the back of his hand with his thumb. Feeling the jagged muscles that grow beneath it. He hovers the handkerchief above the wound before gently pressing it down.

Mydeimos stirs but does not flinch. He grows wary.

When Phainon finishes cleaning the wound and begins to wrap it between layers of glaze, his movements cautious as if Mydeimos would break if he moved too harshly against his skin. Phainon’s touch is not rough or crude. It’s fleeting but remains, making Mydeimos’s skin burn with every touch. Suddenly Phainon's hands pull away but he remains kneeling down.

Mydeimos is the first to talk. “You are more forbearing than I thought.” Offering his hand to the warrior kneeling below. Phainon flashes a grin and takes it, finding his place beside the prince on the edge of the bedside. Not quite letting go of the prince’s hand.

“Did you wish I treated you with such cruelty and animosity instead?” Phainon strokes the palms of Mydeimos’s hand. Exploring the lines that carve out scars.

Mydeimos hums. Not exactly answering Phainon’s question. He stares at Phainon inspecting his scars of bygone battles.

Phainon hesitates before asking, “Do you not find yourself deserving of such gentleness?” His thumb stops tracing a line that runs from Mydeimos’s wrist to his forearm and he peers skyward into Mydeimos’s sunset-colored eyes. He notices the sun-shaped irises within his gaze.

Mydeimos’s voice speaks almost involuntarily, “I have never known it to have wanted it.”

“It’s not a bad thing to want, Mydei. You should do it more so—you are entitled to wanting.”

Am I? Mydeimos thinks. But he has always wanted everything, never being able to obtain it. It blows in the wind, loosening in his grip. Mydeimos thinks and wants, oh how he wants —to live a life outside of a hero, not burdened with the future of becoming the mad god of Strife. But he doesn’t say this, not to Phainon, not to anyone but himself—a silent witness to a beginning neither dared name.

------------

Fragment of Reconciliation: Okhema Holy City, Year 4931, Month of Freedom.

‧︵‿₊୨𖤓୧₊‿︵‧ 

The air in Okhema was joyous, music filling the streets. By the saints, the month blessed by Kephale is one where citizens and heroes alike find themselves at ease. A much-needed one at that—although the flame-chase journey never stops—even the Goldweaver Aglaea can acknowledge the strain it brings. Hence why she had ordered the Chrysos Heirs a moment of leisure.

The only problem, Phainon doesn’t know how to relax.

He finds himself running errands around the Holy City to keep his mind occupied and body moving, doing the opposite of relaxing. Mydei is watching the streets, leg propped against the wall and arms crossed, and that is when he spots him.

Phainon is conversing with citizens near one of the stalls after having helped them lift supplies. To the untrained eyes, Phainon is simply a warrior born with a penchant to help and provide. Mydei notices it though.

He sees the way Phainon moves, exhausted and jaded. His smile never quite reaches his eyes. Mydeimos begins to recall all the times he has seen Phainon look like that. A mirage of facades that crumbles in the corners but never enough to reveal itself to the public.

He, unbeknownst, deep in thought, finds himself staring too long, that Phainon notices him through the crowd and waves to him—causing Mydei to look away and scoff.

Mydei doesn’t see the dejected way Phainon's smile fades slightly.

‧︵‿₊୨𖤓୧₊‿︵‧ 

There’s a hum that sounds when Phainon takes the lift to the Garden of Life. It stops and he steps out onto the pad of grass, the surrounding area empty—for the first time in a while. He doesn’t mind though, the scattering chimeras run up to his feet as he passes them, a soft chuckle escaping him. He settles underneath one of the huts near the edge of the garden, shaded by the tree. Phainon sits down, his blue cape serving as a backdrop for him to sit on, pressing his back against the tree trunk. The rough texture of the wood presses against his clothing, no doubt leaving their patterns onto his skin. His arm rests against his knee as he closes his eyes briefly.

Phainon doesn’t know how long he slept for but there’s a slight scent of pomegranate in the air mixed with wisteria hanging from the garden that entrances his nostrils. He doesn’t question the soft shift of his body when it is moved to lay on something or someone warm, nuzzled on their lap. He doesn’t question the hands in his hair, combing through the tangled buds.

Phainon quite likes this dream.

It feels like home, and reminds him too much of someone. So he continues to sleep despite the knowing pit growing in his stomach that if he awakes now, the dream will end.

‧︵‿₊୨𖤓୧₊‿︵‧ 

Phainon is awakened when something underneath him stirs. His eyes flutter open then instantly shut, the light blinding him. He tries again and this time, a pair of golden eyes greets him. He blinks away his tiredness.

Offhandedly Phainon mutters, “You are like a dream.” Half awake and a little bit too honest. His voice is almost sad.

Mydei’s eyes follow Phainon's expression but he doesn't move Phainon from off his lap.

“A dream..? How so?” Mydei asked him.

“Only in my sleep does everything I wish come true.”

Phainon's hands go to touch Mydeimos’ cheek, lifting it up until he feels the flush of heat rising into his own face, that he hesitates and stops. Hand dropping back down.

Mydeimos continues to look down at Phainon, seeing the rush of emotions flood his face before ultimately settling on one he knows all too well: avoidance.

Phainon, perhaps embarrassed now, goes to sit up, pressing himself up on his forearms but Mydeimos pushes him back down. His eyes are almost glassy and hazy, unsure of Mydei's action. Before he can go to question him. Mydei says, “Your dream. What did you dream about?”

A distraction, but nevertheless Phainon doesn’t try to leave again and relaxes slightly against Mydeimos' lap.

I dreamt of you. But Phainon doesn’t say that, he still doesn’t believe any of this is real. So he asks, not a question, but rather a statement.

“Mydeimos, you don’t have to do this… I am well.”

“Yes, I know. But Lady Aglaea has given command for leisure, but you know no means of getting rest. I‘ll stay to keep you here until you’ve proved otherwise.”

A quiet silence, then laughter from the white-haired man.

“You will... accompany me as I sleep?”

“You owe me company for missing our evening spar, so this will do.”

“Ah... apologies, I must have forgotten.”

Mydeimos nods silently but doesn’t seem to press the matter. He’s looking off into the distance as Phainon's eyes trace the features of Mydeimos’ face from where he’s laying. He can see the sharp curve of his chin, the delicate muscles of his jaw—everything Phainon once dreamt of before.

Phainon's mouth opens before shutting, the words dying in his throat. Mydei seems to notice this too.

“Deliverer, ask for what you want.”

“It’s a selfish want.”

“Then be selfish once in a while.”

Phainon smiles, remembering Mydei’s words in his mind.

“I wish to stay here a while, if you don’t mind being my pillow.” He laughs.

Mydeimos’ fist hits Phainon on the head lightly. Phainon's hand goes to cover Mydei from knocking into him more but Mydei doesn’t. Instead, he speaks, “Sleep, Deliverer.”

A silent acknowledgment of intimacy being found, but they don’t say anything—keeping this dream real and concealed.

------------

Fragment of Reconciliation: Okhema Holy City, Year 4932, Month of Gate. 

‧︵‿₊୨ ☾𖤓୧₊‿︵‧ 

“Did you hear, tonight is the night of parting. The Crown Prince of Castrum Kremnos leaves the holy city tonight.”

“What of his people? How shall they fare without their ruler?”

“What of his lover, Lord Phainon? Shall he accompany Prince Mydeimos on his journey home?”

“I wasn’t aware of their courtship. Perhaps they meant to keep it wary from public eyes?”

Lovers? Were the two ever truly lovers? A camaraderie formed between damaged, kindred spirits—tiptoeing the line of duty and love. Yet, they are not quite friends and not quite lovers. A blurry middle that they dare not name— naming things makes it real. And they cannot be. Should not be. For time is a cruel thing, it hinders them with the intention of wanting, and they cannot want. They do not ask to be loved because asking means to receive, and they cannot burden each other with the task to love them. So they exist, shoulder to shoulder, indulging in what little time does remain. Their relationship treads the lines of impossibility and viability—but Oronyx is unfair and grants them neither.

Mydeimos and Phainon do not speak of the rumors that spread throughout the Holy City—and if they have heard them—they do not discuss the matter.

‧︵‿₊୨ ☾𖤓୧₊‿︵‧

The night before parting is festive. The Seamstress set forth a grand banquet, one worthy of a king—in honor of Mydeimos’ grand return home to guard the frontline. Marmoreal Market is bustling with Okheman and Kremnoan alike, and from the rooftops anchored with layers of colored drapes, Mydeimos stood looking over the noise of the effervescent city. From this view, Mydeimos’ vision blurred as he stared at the people walking the streets.

Okhema, shall now be home to my people.

But Mydeimos’ pondering came to an unexpected end when the metal rail he leaned against shook, as someone took a place beside him.

Mydeimos continued to watch the citizens below, the intermingling of life going on around them. He does not need to see who stands beside him. Because he knows, he always does. Mydeimos knows from the light footsteps that settle beside him, he hears it in the way that he breathes, and the way his clothing flows in the wind. He doesn’t turn because it is Phainon.

“It’s a festival in the name of the Crown Prince and you do not wish to join in on the occasion?” Phainon says. His voice is airy and honeyed. “Lady Aglaea went through all the trouble just for the guest of honor to disappear halfway through.” Phainon gives off a faint laugh and Mydeimos hears the way Phainon breathes in.

Mydeimos’ gaze turns to look at Phainon but Phainon’s eyes remain distantly distracted, glancing toward somewhere beyond. Phainon’s right hand holds on to the railing, while the other lays by his side. His face was solemn with a hint of solace emanating from his eyes, an unusual expression for a man like Phainon. Mydeimos thinks it doesn’t suit him. “If it is the Crown Prince you’re looking for, then you need not trouble yourself.”

“Oh?” A hint of surprise in the man’s voice. Phainon’s smile turns into a mischievous grin. Phainon turns to look at Mydeimos, finally locking eyes onto the color of gold.

“Right now, I shall enjoy myself just as Mydeimos. Not the Crown Prince, the Demi-god of Strife—just—”

“Just Mydei.” A gentle smile graces Phainon’s lips as he finishes Mydeimos’ sentence. Mydeimos stares blankly at the man, before he hums in agreement.

The air is hot and dazed, steam rising from the food stalls and the breeze drunk with alcohol. A passing, yet comfortable silence.

Mydeimos shifted his balance slightly before leaning forward on the railing, arms hanging out as his forearm touched and fell upon the surface of the stone rails. Mydeimos’ voice is rough and humorous when he speaks, “What made you so faint on this fine night, Deliverer?”

Perhaps it was the booze in the air that caused them both to fumble their words and movements, or the way Phainon turns to look Mydeimos in the eyes with a look so full of emotion—an emotion they both have felt sparkled yet buried beneath friendship and fear. But right now, Phainon’s eyes are full of it—that tingling and hot sensation Mydeimos feels whenever Phainon is near.

“Say, Mydei,” Phainon’s voice wavers before he clears his throat. “Would you allow me to be selfish for a moment?”

Selfish? Mydeimos thinks. A funny thing, really. A man like Phainon declaring himself as selfish? It’s laughable at best.

Mydeimos scoffs. “You? Say what—” He goes to say more before Phainon closes the distance between them, walking closer to where he was. His body is close to Mydeimos and Phainon’s hand goes to brace his wrist. “Deliverer, what game are you playing?”

When he realizes Phainon is not stopping his approach, Mydeimos instantly takes a step backward. He steadies himself on the rails, letting go before realizing Phainon had caught him within his grasp—hindering Mydeimos, unable to move further.

Phainon’s eyes are distant and firm before he speaks, “Forgive me, Mydei.” Then suddenly Phainon leans in, placing a chaste kiss on Mydeimos’ lips.

Mydeimos’ breath hitches. Body stunned, his eyes widening upon Phainon’s taste upon his lips.

Phainon’s grip on Mydeimos’ wrist loosens but he does not move, not yet. The rustling of the wind is loud compared to the silence that now accompanies them on the rooftops. “Mydei, I—”

But Mydeimos is confused. He continues to stare at Phainon, as he sheepishly smiles, rubbing a hand against the back of his neck. It causes him to tussle his hair in a way that looks so soft.

Phainon is speaking some words to Mydeimos yet he cannot hear it over the pounding of his heart or the fear growing in his eyes. Mydeimos’ hand that lay dormant at his side raises up slowly, his fingers delicately touching his lips as if he could still feel the warmth of Phainon’s lips on his own.

Had he really kissed me? Does he…

Something in Mydeimos broke and he staggered away. Finally pulling back and breaking free from Phainon’s touch. Phainon stops his words and a look—that Mydeimos can’t quite see clearly—has fallen upon his face. Mydeimos, unable to bear what Phainon’s expression may be, turns and leaves. He doesn’t spare a glance back. A hasty exit despite the shouts of protest coming from the other. At once, Mydeimos is making his way down the roof and finds himself converging within the crowd.

He rushes past them, as the crowd turns to notice just who is passing by. They step aside to make room for the Crown Prince and long after Mydeimos has passed they see a figure of a white-haired man following after. Rumors and gossip begin to circle once more.

‧︵‿₊୨ ☾𖤓୧₊‿︵‧

Underneath the colonnade bridge, Mydeimos steadies his steps, passing pillar by pillar. Action hour begins to follow, yet Mydeimos finds himself distracted. He pauses and momentarily glances at the dawn device held up together by Kephale. He’s reminded of a certain someone again. He shakes his head to break out of that thought but it doesn’t leave him, not yet. He slows himself and breathes. Unable to get that feeling out of his chest. He wonders if the gods could hear the pounding of his heart against his ribs, for it beats so fast and unsteady. Uncertain and fearful, a feeling he knows all too well.

Mydeimos is away from the crowd, alone as time passes by. His hands go to trace his lips once more. His index and middle fingers travel lightly on the surface of his blushed lips. He could still feel that fleeting sensation growing. Just then, Mydeimos hears someone approach and turns to the noise, dropping his hands from his lips.

“Mydeimos…” Phainon’s voice echoing through the colonnade. Mydeimos defensively straightens.

“Deliverer, a bold move that was—but to think you’d follow me, you—”

“There’s…to say, I…managed to finally catch…up with you…” A breathless and tired Phainon speaks, words flowing out. “You didn’t let me finish what I had left unsaid.”

“No.”

“No?” Phainon’s chest is heaving, rising up and down as he pants. His back is bent forward, a hand resting on his thigh as he slouches.

Mydeimos’ eyebrows furrow and he watches Phainon closely. Phainon doesn’t move from where he stands but he goes to lift his hand as if to reach out to Mydeimos. Mydeimos only stares at it like it has offended him. It drops back down.

“You say I should speak more freely, ask for what I want. I ask for you to listen.”

And isn’t that cruel? To use Mydeimos’ words against him in this way.

He gives a gentle laugh before fondly continuing, “Could the rumors… be true? The great Mydeimos, himself, has fallen in love with another? Pray tell, who in Okhema could have captured your heart?” His tone betrays how his eyes waver, the realization further splitting the rift between his heart.

“Don’t tell me you indulge in idle gossip.”

“Only when it involves you.” And Mydeimos can hear the smile on Phainon’s lips when he speaks.

Mydeimos’ mouth opens to retort, to laugh, or scoff, but he finds himself unable to speak. He inhales, looking at how Phainon is bathed in gold from the dawn peeking over the horizon. 

“Then speak,” Mydeimos' voice is determined yet distant. “Say what you must.”

“Is that all you have to say? After…” Phainon’s mind lingers back to their shared kiss, and his cheeks flush a tint of rosy pink. He covers his mouth with his hand, tearing his eyes away from Mydeimos’ flat expression.

Phainon doesn’t need to say it for Mydeimos to understand what he’s hinting at. Mydeimos’ eyes flinch at the memory, a bit of heat rising into his own cheeks.

“Mydei.” And Mydeimos looks up to see Phainon again. His expression is full of resolve by the way he speaks Mydeimos’ name. “Didn’t I say you should allow yourself the freedom to want? I ask you this: do you want me, Mydeimos?” Phainon’s voice is quiet and anguished.

Somewhere else, perhaps several years earlier, they had already crossed lines that should have never been crossed. Yet, like a moth drawn into a raging flame, they burn for each other—time and time again—just to feel their hearts ignite beneath the other's touch.

“Do not speak those words.” Mydeimos’ voice is sharp.

“Why?”

“You cannot.”

Phainon takes a hesitant step forward—then another, more confident—and another, until Mydeimos steps back with each advancement until he hits a pillar behind him.

“Are you afraid?” Afraid of wanting , Phainon means to say, but it goes unspoken.

Phainon’s arm props against the pillar beside Mydeimos’ head as he leans in closer until their breaths mingle. They do not break eye contact, and so Mydeimos speaks.

“We are friends.”

“Is that what we are? Nothing more?”

“That is all.”

Mydeimos’ heart skips a beat. And Phainon, being Phainon, pushes the matter further until he sees the transparency of Mydeimos’ own aching, bleeding heart.

“Do friends kiss beneath starlight, or search for a moment’s glance from the other in every crowd or corner? Do they savor the way their name is spoken upon a holy tongue? Do they dream of ravaging each other and whispering words of dishonor, all the while wanting to taste them on their skin?”

Phainon inches closer, until his lips graze over Mydeimos’, and he tilts his head slightly. His eyes glance once at Mydeimos’ lips before returning to his gaze.

“Are their minds eroded with wanting more than what they settle for, all for the familiar notion of keeping that comfortability?”

Phainon’s hand goes to cup Mydeimos’ cheek, then slips past, instead tucking a loose strand of hair behind his ear.

This time Mydeimos turns and looks away, his voice uncharacteristically soft, “You speak as if you are in love with me.”

“And if I am?”

A gentle hand turns Mydeimos’ chin, but his eyes are locked onto the sun tattoo sitting beneath Phainon’s collar. Instinctively, Mydeimos goes to touch it.

Phainon leans into the touch, pushing his neck against Mydeimos’ palm. “We—” he begins before taking a deep breath.

We don’t have the luxury of becoming more, Mydeimos thinks. He exhales.

“We have duties bound by the prophecy. We don't have the luxury of wanting, Deliverer.” And Mydeimos believes it. He cannot love Phainon fully in a cruel world bound by but a lifetime of separation. So he waits—for the next lifetime perhaps, or forever—somewhere between now and then, for a time where they do not have to choose between love and duty for the Era Nova.

Phainon knows it too. They cannot abandon their duty to the Flame Chase. But the heart is a selfish, childish thing. It goes where it wants without knowing the consequences, yearning to be loved and to love. It cries out for their other half to fulfill theirs.

“Just this once, let me choose love.” He nuzzles against Mydeimos’ hand, then places his own atop it.

And in the next cycles after this, where duty is not needed, I’ll choose love. For you, for a chance where we can exist.

Phainon whispers, “Okay?”

“Okay.”

His hand trails down Mydeimos’ forearm, caressing it carefully, his thumb rubbing against Mydeimos’ pulse. How fast it beats under Phainon’s touch. He tilts his head to the side, and when he sees Mydeimos has no intention to run from him again, he closes the distance between them—giving Mydeimos time to deny him if he wishes—before swooning in and kissing him, deep, messy, and passionately. Mydeimos’ hand moves from Phainon’s neck to rest on his shoulder, his other hand finding its way into Phainon’s hair, gripping it tightly—Phainon’s snowy white hair now tangled in the fingers of Mydeimos’ hand. Phainon pushes forward, earning a groan that escapes Mydeimos’ lips as his whole body knocks into the pillar behind him fully.

They gasp and break off to catch their breath. Mydeimos’ lips are bitten and red, glistening with saliva. Phainon thinks he looks beautiful and leans back in, before they hear conversation nearby. Across the bridge, people begin to approach. Yet, Phainon—unaware or uncaring—goes back to minding his business with his beloved.

Before he can kiss Mydeimos once more, a hand is pressed against his chest, near his heart—as if stopping him.

Mydeimos’ voice is raspy and dire, “People will stare.”

“Let them stare. Eyes were made to look.” Phainon’s hands move to his waist, pulling Mydeimos lightly toward his own chest before kissing him intensely, as their mouths slot together.

‧︵‿₊୨ ☾𖤓୧₊‿︵‧

Mydeimos does not remember the walk to his chambers. Once they broke from their kiss, as if by some unspoken agreement, Phainon straddled him along the stone path before slipping into Mydeimos’ bedchamber. Comfortable silence followed by fingers intertwined all the way.

But he does remember the way Phainon says his name, the way Phainon’s Okheman accent traces each syllable of it. My-Dee-Mos.

Mydeimos…

How Mydeimos loved the way it sounded coming from his mouth rather than his own.

Once the click of the door closed and locked behind them, Phainon’s hands gave way, cupping Mydeimos’ face in his own. Unwavering, endless blues dilating into his amber ones.

“Mydeimos?” A flustered voice calling for him, making Mydeimos pipe back into reality.

“I am here. Don’t worry.”

Phainon’s embarrassment is shown on his face, but he asks a rather simple yet needless question. “May I kiss you?”

Mydei laughs at the unnecessary question. When he peers back into Phainon’s eyes, he thinks he can see the uncertainty beneath the surface of those unmoving ocean waves, and so he indulges him. “You have already. No need to ask for what is yours.”

“Mine?” A cheeky smile gracing Phainon’s face. “Does that make you mine as well, Mydeimos?”

“Nevermind then.” Already starting to pull away from Phainon’s hands on his face.

“No, please, I jest,” a lighthearted laugh comes from the man. “I’ll take you up on that offer. I shall kiss you all over.”

Mydeimos hums in amusement. Phainon’s hands finding their way to his neck and back, kissing once on Mydei’s head, cheek, then lips—this one longer and more intense. The force is so strong they knock into the leg of the bed, throwing them off balance. Phainon grips Mydei’s body closer to him, keeping them from falling entirely. They lean, hovering beside the foot of the bed, the alluded implication hanging in the air.

Mydeimos’ heart stops. Phainon, who leans toward him, is stopped when Mydei’s hand goes to cover Phainon’s mouth from reaching his lips. He stops, afraid of having hurt Mydeimos, concern and fear in his face. He is about to ask—ask again—if Mydei wishes to stop, but Mydei beats him to it.

“Phainon.” And Phainon knows it’s serious because Mydeimos said his name and not his title of Deliverer.

“Do you wish to stop, Mydeimos?”

Mydeimos flushes a deep shade of red, creeping into his ears. “Phainon…” he says again. “I have never…I’ve never taken…a lover before.” He turns away from Phainon before pausing. “So…I am inexperienced in the matter of…consummation.” Mydei’s voice is quiet and hesitant, as he pushes the words out slowly.

Phainon’s eyes widened and mouth fell open, out of surprise more than anything.

“Does that bother you?” Mydei’s voice questioning and a bit embarrassed.

Phainon’s lips close and Mydei can feel him smile in his palm. Mydei drops his hand covering Phainon’s mouth and turns to examine his reaction, eyes watching and waiting.

“No.” His smile can be heard when he speaks. He grabs Mydei’s wrist and places a kiss inside his palm. “You are my first, as well.”

My first and only lover.

And Mydeimos’ flush grows more at Phainon’s admission. Phainon’s laughter is piercing and radiant, cutting through the air, and suddenly they fall onto the sheets of the bed. Phainon supports himself before his body crashes into Mydei, who now lays beneath him. Mydei’s breathing is heavy and Phainon can only observe the sight from above. Mydeimos’ hair sprawled like a backdrop against the velvet red sheets, cheeks a rosy red, and hazy eyes growing with desire and want.

The only sound that could be heard was their heavy breathing, seeping in like the dawn peeking through after a rainy day.

Phainon admires Mydeimos, looking up and down, as he is a sight to behold underneath him. They grow hot and feel their body heat mix, sweat making their clothing stick to their skin.

“May I?” His hand presses gently against Mydeimos’ chest, fingers holding the edge of his robe, waiting for permission from the one Phainon calls his. Mydei nods. “I am going to undress you now.” He places a kiss at the corner of his mouth before slowly and gently pulling off fabric and armor. He does this until they both lay bare for one another to see. “I’m going to…make love to you now, Mydeimos.” The man under him flushes a darker shade and reluctantly nods, not because Mydei isn’t sure but rather because he doesn't know what it’s like to be treated with such care. In the way Phainon asks—because of course he does—before doing, because he knows it is Mydei’s first . First at  everything intimate and gentle. First at knowing love. First time giving his heart away to someone, knowing he might never get it back. But Phainon does, he gives and gives until Mydeimos learns to receive that love, his love. 

And Mydeimos is sorry about that. For he knows that Phainon will have to always keep giving and giving in this life and the next as the bearer of the world. He’s sorry for not being able to realize his feelings before having to part ways forever. 

There’s a warm and fuzzy feeling that welts up in Mydeimos’ stomach when Phainon enters him. Mydei’s forearm rests against his forehead, his nails digging into his palm as Phainon moves further in, deeper and deeper. His other hand wraps around the nape of the white haired warrior. At first there’s a rush of adrenaline and Phainon can tell from the subtle knowing look on Mydei’s face, that he is in pain. Phainon knows that look. He sees glances of it in passing, that look adorning his face especially in quiet solitude. 

Phainon panics, “Oh, Mydeimos..have I hurt you?” His words spilling out quickly in a whisper, like one would hear when singing a lullaby. Mydei’s forearm shifts, moving to cover his eyes to hide from Phainon piercing eyes looming above him. His eyes fall shut and his features twist as he stabilizes himself to adjust to a different type of pain—not from vengeance and violence—one that is sweet and kind, only with the intent of passion, desire, and want. 

“No…I am alright. You are kind to me, I just—”

I’m not used to this, especially from someone like you.

Phainon doesn’t relax as he watches Mydeimos wince once more. The scent of blood still in the air—the loss of purity—broken between them. He lightly grabs Mydeimos’ forearm, pulling it away to see his face. Mydei doesn’t resist. Phainon places it above Mydei’s head, pinning it in place. “I want to see you.” 

Mydei opens his eyes, adjusting to the light again and he sees tears forming in Phainon’s sapphire eyes.

Mydei’s hand previously on Phainon’s nape finds its way to his cheek, wiping away the beads of tears protruding at the corner, that have yet to fall. 

“Phainon..do not cry, you have not harmed me. It’s alright. Please..continue to keep me company tonight”

That's Mydei's own way of saying, please don’t go. I wish to spend my last moment with you. Mydeimos, taking the initiative, pulls Phainon forward, kissing him tenderly until he feels the light breeze of Phainon lashes falling shut. 

Phainon doesn’t tell Mydeimos the tears he shed was because this would be the last and only time they could ever want. He cried because he’ll miss Mydei when he goes. 

The beads of tears trickled down making their way to where their lips met, Mydei tasting the salt and deepening the kiss as if to say, I wish to have all of you. 

A scuffle among the sheets, legs tangled together with sounds meant only for the other to hear, filled the room. 

Let their love be sealed tonight. As proof that they too, once loved each other in this lifetime. The drop of blood that soaked into the bed sheets as they drowned in each other and lost chastity was given—all on the Crown Prince’s last night in Okhema’s Holy City.

In the next lifetime, Mydeimos. I’ll choose you once more.

There will be stories of their battles and hardships passed down into the new world. But they will never be written in the tales of epics or stories, retelling their love for each other. Not as friends nor lovers—just as Phainon and Mydeimos, two heroes of Amphoreus. Their romance is only remembered through the time of Oronyx’s powers, capturing a story they never got to write.

Let’s meet again in the new world, Phainon. I’ll be sure to love you properly.

May their duty in the next life be dedicated solely to each other.

‧︵‿₊୨ ☾𖤓୧₊‿︵‧

chapters.title: Afterword
chapters.html:
End Notes

Are they lovers?
Worse. They never got to be.
Yet, they need not be lovers to know love. For if that was true, they would have been lovers their whole lives.
When you’re in a Greek yearning competition and these fools show up—it’s over. I hope you enjoy reading! Each fragment is meant to capture a moment in Mydei and Phainon’s relationship and how it slowly progresses over the 1–3 years before the main storyline, leading up to Mydei’s departure to the frontlines. As I was writing, I felt the more I wrote about Phainon and Mydeimos’ intimacy, especially in private, I felt like I was intruding because their love was only ever meant for each other. That’s why I wrote their sexual intimacy as vague and non-explicit because even we, the audience, cannot bear witness to how they love. Only they know.
They know love, they have love—but they’ve never had the time or freedom to truly become lovers.

{Summary of key points per memory fragments/importance of what each month symbolizes}
The month of Strife represents consistent battle and conflict. Mydei is the bearer of the Coreflame of Strife and has been taught only to destroy. His hands aren't meant to cradle. Mydei does not know gentleness. Phainon treats Mydei like he deserves to feel it.

The month of Freedom is a month granted by Kephale, where citizens of Okhema have time to pursue hobbies and indulge in leisure activities. Phainon doesn’t always tend to care for himself, and Mydeimos bothers him about it. Phainon learns that asking isn’t always a selfish thing.

The Month of Gate represents people letting go of their past and stepping forward towards a brighter future. Typically, people would burn or discard things from the past. Symbolizes Phainon and Mydei embracing their requited love before letting go to forge a new dawn for the Era Nova—in their next life, they can hopefully be lovers without sacrificing themselves for duty.
